title: Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that there is an absolute constant c > 0 with (1 - beta) log q >= c for every real zero beta in (0,1) of the L-function of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet character of conductor q >= 3, the logarithmic form of the Landau-Siegel problem. A real zero close to 1 leaves few primes with chi(p) = 1 up to a large power of q (a short argument with the logarithmic derivatives of zeta and L). Polynomials with separately bounded degrees take arbitrary values on a linear image of an integer box in C^4 (a dimension count, a nearest-point argument for an integer polytope and Lagrange interpolation on a face). In the biquadratic field Q(sqrt d, sqrt 2), rows of products of three conjugates chosen by a weighted order give a nonzero determinant whose degree lies mostly in one conjugate. Its norm is bounded above by Hadamard's inequality and below by divisibility at the primes p > H with chi(p) = -1, where the Frobenius congruence holds; the two bounds differ by the factor 3/4 = log N/log U. A zero-free region with no exceptional zero follows.
prerequisites: complex analysis and Dirichlet L-functions as in the programme courses The Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions, cited at each use
linear algebra over a field: determinants, rank, Hadamard's inequality

No error was found. Changes of form in the course: (1) explicit constants in the analytic part: -zeta'/zeta(s) < 1/(s-1) + 1 for real s > 1 from the integral formula for zeta, and Gamma'/Gamma(3/2) = 2 - gamma - 2 log 2, giving the prime bias with the constant e and the mass bound with 4 log q, 3 delta (log X)^2/log q and log H + 2 c_M; (2) the face argument uses G = conv(S cap G) and Caratheodory's theorem directly, without vertices, and bounds the dimension of the face by the hyperplane h.v = max; (3) the final step fixes H = 86,713,344 and N = ceil(q^55) explicitly; (4) Corollary B, a zero-free region without exception, is derived from the programme's classical region; (5) a remark shows that the leading terms coincide at 3/4 when the primes with Frobenius 1 are added, so that without a real zero there is no contradiction, and exact computed examples show that the divisibility fails at primes with Frobenius tau and can fail at p <= H. Follow-up literature read on 17 Oct 2026: Banks, arXiv:2610.15483 (explicit constants, 3.0e-3 for q >= 10^10); Kerr, arXiv:2610.21099 (pigeonhole and Masser's zero estimate instead of the interpolation determinant); Kimura, arXiv:2610.21511 (5.8e-4 for all q >= 3, Lean, imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000). None reports an error in the argument.
